top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength lattice is a separable idea from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion control: it cancels the differential light shift while holding thousands of atoms Doppler- and recoil-free, taking accuracy from the 1e-15 range to about 1e-18. The shifts are understood and the performance is reproduced across independent laboratories and intercontinental links, so the work is mature. Two names (Katori for the proposal and first Sr lattice clock, Ye for the accuracy frontier and many-body clock) match the record. The citation should name the lattice and lead with capability rather than constants tests, which have so far been null.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I work in atomic, molecular and optical physics at Lund but have no apparent direct tie to Katori or Ye
